c.tagline: The quiet Aegean town beside the vast ruins of ancient Ephesus and the Temple of Artemis
langs: English (widely spoken due to Ephesus tourism)

card: Widely accepted at hotels and restaurants; small local shops and the Saturday market may prefer cash.
rides: dolmuş minibuses to Ephesus and Kuşadası

taxi.fare: Roughly ₺30-50 flag fall plus metered per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: A fixed rate is common for the short trip to Ephesus's Upper or Lower Gate

walk: Selçuk town center is small and walkable, with the fortress and basilica within easy reach; Ephesus itself is a short dolmuş or taxi ride, and Şirince requires a short drive.

safety.safety: Very safe for solo travelers, including women; Selçuk is a quiet, tourist-friendly town centered on the Ephesus site
safety.crime: Petty theft is rare; standard caution applies around the busy Ephesus site entrances

hood_landmark.Selçuk Town Center: Ayasuluk Fortress and the Basilica of St. John
hood_landmark.Şirince: Şirince's stone village and vineyard restaurants
hood_landmark.Pamucak: Pamucak Beach, the long open sand strip west of Selcuk

avoid.reason: Persistent carpet and souvenir touts work the Ephesus gates and station area; agree taxi fares beforehand.

hood_desc: The compact town center below Ayasuluk hill, with the fortress, basilica ruins, Saturday market, and most of the guesthouses.
A picturesque Greek-heritage stone village in the hills above Selçuk, known for fruit wines and terrace restaurants.

A flat stretch of open sand on the Aegean about 7 km west of Selcuk, at the mouth of the Kucuk Menderes, backed by a handful of large all-inclusive beach resorts and almost nothing else; a car or the dolmus is needed to reach the town and Ephesus.

water.note: Stick to bottled water, as most locals do.

transit.sys: Dolmuş (shared minibus) network connecting Selçuk to Ephesus, Kuşadası, and Şirince
transit.map: Dolmuş depart from the Selçuk otogar near the train station
transit.note: Walking or a short dolmuş ride covers most sights; Ephesus has two gates (Upper and Lower) worth knowing for a one-way walking tour

transport.air: Izmir Adnan Menderes Airport (ADB), about 60 km away, has domestic and international flights
transport.train: Selçuk station has regional rail connections to Izmir
transport.bus: Regional coaches connect Selçuk to Izmir, Kuşadası, and other Aegean towns
transport.ferry: None — Selçuk itself is a few km inland; nearest ferry access is via Kuşadası
transport.car: Self-driving is convenient for reaching Şirince, Pamucak, and the Ephesus site gates independently

airport.name: Izmir Adnan Menderes Airport
airport.transport: Regional train or bus via Izmir; taxi transfer roughly $45-60

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.fwn: Free wifi widely available in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Turkcell or Vodafone tourist SIM or eSIM is recommended

tip.r: 10% is standard at restaurants where service isn't already included

landmarks: Ephesus Ancient City
One of the Mediterranean's greatest classical cities, this sprawling UNESCO-listed Roman metropolis of marble streets, temples and terraced houses lies just outside town.
Library of Celsus
Ephesus's show-stopping two-storey facade of columns and statues, built around 117 AD, is among the most photographed ruins in the ancient world.
Great Theatre of Ephesus
A colossal 25,000-seat Roman amphitheatre carved into Mount Pion where St. Paul preached, still hosting occasional concerts with sweeping harbour-road views.
Temple of Artemis
A lone re-erected column and scattered foundations mark one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, once the largest temple in antiquity.
House of the Virgin Mary (Meryemana)
A serene stone chapel on Bülbül Mountain, revered by Christians and Muslims alike as the place where Mary spent her final years.
Basilica of St. John
Hilltop ruins of the great 6th-century Byzantine basilica built by Justinian over the traditional tomb of John the Apostle, with views across Selçuk.
Ayasuluk Castle
A restored Byzantine-Ottoman fortress crowning Ayasuluk Hill above the basilica, its ramparts offering panoramic views over the plain to the Aegean.
İsa Bey Mosque
An elegant 1375 Seljuk-era mosque of contrasting stone with a graceful arcaded courtyard, standing between Ayasuluk Hill and the Artemis temple site.
Ephesus Archaeological Museum
Selçuk's superb museum displays treasures excavated at Ephesus, including the famous multi-breasted marble statues of Artemis of Ephesus.
Şirince Village
A postcard-pretty hillside village of whitewashed Greek houses, cobbled lanes and fruit-wine tastings, an easy and hugely popular excursion from Selçuk.

train.note: No international trains. Selçuk station is on the İzmir-Denizli regional line, a short walk from the centre and about 3 km from Ephesus, with several trains a day to İzmir Basmane in roughly 1h20 and onward services toward Denizli for Pamukkale. Book on TCDD e-bilet from 15 days out; the İzmir suburban İZBAN network also reaches nearby Tepeköy.

bus.note: No international coaches. Selçuk's small otogar in the middle of town has frequent dolmuş minibuses to Kuşadası (about 30 minutes) and Şirince, plus intercity coaches to İzmir, Bodrum, Pamukkale and overnight services to Istanbul on Pamukkale (https://www.pamukkale.com.tr/) and Kamil Koç (https://www.kamilkoc.com.tr/). Book through obilet (https://www.obilet.com/en/).

ferry.note: Selçuk is a few kilometres inland - ancient Ephesus was a port but the harbour silted up centuries ago - so there are no ferries here. The nearest sailings are the Samos boats from Kuşadası, half an hour away by dolmuş.

half.name: Priene, Miletus, and Didyma
half.blurb: Three ancient Ionian cities along the coast, with a hillside theater, a former harbor city, and the massive Temple of Apollo.

half.name: Izmir
half.blurb: Turkey's third-largest city, a port on the Aegean with a bazaar, an ancient agora, and a seafront promenade.

full.name: Pamukkale
full.blurb: White travertine terraces of mineral-rich thermal pools cascade down a hillside beside the ruins of ancient Hierapolis.
